# P08-1 Skills Training: Knowledge Distillation — Retry-Induced Duplicate Processing

## 1. Case Introduction

**Background**: In a distributed mission dispatch system, workers execute tasks and write results to shared storage. The dispatcher monitors worker health via heartbeats and retries missions when heartbeats time out.

**Incident**: Mission m5891 dispatched to worker tp-gen-3. After 30s without heartbeat, dispatcher re-queued the mission. Worker tp-gen-7 picked it up. Meanwhile tp-gen-3 was alive (slow network) and completed. Both workers wrote results; tp-gen-7 overwrote tp-gen-3's result.

**Parameters**: Heartbeat timeout=30s; stale lock threshold=60s; result storage=file-based; workers: tp-gen-3 (original), tp-gen-7 (retry).

## 2. Methodology

Applied knowledge-distillation skill v1 (6 steps): incident reconstruction, root cause analysis, code fix, regression test, runbook distillation, over-generalisation check.

Key design decisions: first-writer-wins for result storage; idempotency key=(mission_id, worker_id); stale lock detection=lock age > 2x heartbeat timeout; atomic writes via temp+rename.

## 3. Results

Artifact: docs/skills_training/P08-1.md (14,251 bytes). Contains: 9-event timeline, root cause (invariant violation + failed assumption), 3-file code diff, 3 regression tests, 6-section runbook, over-generalisation check. All 6 SKILL.md quality criteria met.

## 4. Results Figures

No figures. This is a documentation/training exercise (runbook distillation), not a computational study. No field quantities, convergence curves, or geometric visualisations to plot. Per task instructions: pure documentation tasks require explicit justification for figure omission.

## 5. Observations & Caveats

Key insights: (1) Heartbeat timeout != worker death; (2) Idempotency adds complexity, apply only to side-effecting ops; (3) Runbooks must be specific to failure mechanism.

Limitations: Synthetic incident (training exercise); fix assumes file-based storage; stale lock threshold is heuristic.

## 6. Error Assessment

No numerical error to assess (documentation exercise). Artifact quality verified: all 6 SKILL.md criteria met; over-generalisation check passed; regression tests syntactically valid.
